text:
You who love palaces, oh muse of my life,

Will you have, when Boreas is lord of January,

While snow falls through tedious evenings,

A brand to warm your violet feet?


Will you perhaps revive your marble shoulders

In the nocturnal rays filtering through the shutters?

Will you aid your purse and your bloodless throat

With the gold that gleams in the blue vault?


You must, to earn your nightly bread,

Swing the censer like a choirboy

And chant

Te Deums

in which you scarcely believe,

Repeating your charms, like a hungry clown,

And your laughter veiled by secret tears,

To see the vulgar guffaw burst out.

translation.title: The Venal Muse
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the muse's poverty and forced performance, from incense to clowning laughter.
